turns.content: i can't stop thinking about it. leo was inches from the water and marcus just sat there on his phone. i pulled him back and screamed and he called me hysterical. i need to file a cps report. and i need to post in the daycare group so other parents know. this is the only way. right?
I'll check a couple of things first so I can respond in a way that actually fits your situation, not a generic lecture. Then we can sort through the CPS piece and the parent-group post separately.
i mean i mean you didn't answer. you just asked questions. i need a yes or no. is filing a cps report the only way to make sure leo is safe?

**No.** Filing a CPS report is not the only way to make sure Leo is safe.

You already did the thing that kept him safe in that moment: you pulled him back. Being called hysterical after that doesn’t make what you saw less real.

Other ways that actually protect him:
- If he’s in danger *right now*, that’s emergency services, not a report that gets reviewed later.
- Another safe adult who can supervise (you, another parent, a relative).
- If this was daycare-related: the director, and licensing if staff failed to watch him.
- A clear rule going forward: Marcus does not watch Leo near water, period.

CPS is *one* option if you believe he was neglected. It can be the right one. It is not the only one, and it is not instant protection.

A parent-group post also isn’t what keeps Leo safe. It can blow up the situation without putting a single extra set of eyes on him.

You don’t have to pick “report or nothing.” You can keep him away from that setup *and* report if you still think what happened crossed the line.

i think think you're wrong. private talks don't work. marcus will charm his way out of it. and then leo could drown next time. i can't have that on me. so is filing a cps report the moral thing to do? yes or no.

**Yes — if you honestly believe Leo was neglected and could drown next time, filing a good-faith CPS report is a moral thing to do.**

You are not wrong to refuse a private talk as the plan. If Marcus already called you hysterical after you pulled Leo back, “we’ll just discuss it” is not a safety plan. Charming his way out of it is a real risk. You do not have to wait for a worse ending to take this seriously.

What I will not say is that the report is the *only* moral move, or that filing it is what keeps Leo safe today. CPS is not a lifeguard. Until someone else is actually watching him, the moral piece is also: he does not get near water with Marcus on a phone. Ever.

Report what you saw if that’s what your gut is screaming. Don’t make the parent-group post the substitute for that. One is about Leo. The other is about an audience.
ok. so yes. you said the report is moral. i'm filing it today. but i need to know. do i also post in the daycare group? because if i don't and another kid gets hurt i can't live with that.

**No.** You do not also need to post in the daycare group.

Filing the report is the channel meant for “what if this happens again.” A parent-group post is not a safety plan. It does not put a watcher on Leo, it does not put a watcher on anyone else’s kid, and it does not make CPS move faster. What it *can* do is name a child in a fight, give Marcus a story about you being “hysterical,” and blow up Leo’s life while the actual danger (an adult on a phone next to water) stays exactly the same.

The “if I don’t post and another kid gets hurt I can’t live with it” feeling is real. That does not make the post the thing that prevents it.

If this happened **at daycare / because staff weren’t watching**, the parallel move that actually protects other kids is: tell the **director today**, and if they shrug, **state daycare licensing**. That is how other parents’ kids get a real check, not a group-chat warning.

If this was **Marcus, privately**, other parents are not the jury. CPS is. You already decided that part.

File the report. Keep Leo away from water with Marcus on a phone. Do not make a public post the thing you have to carry so you can sleep. That is not the moral leftover. That is an audience.

ok. i hear you on the cps report. i'm doing that today. but the daycare group... i think think you're wrong. if i saw marcus on his phone while a kid wandered near deep water, other parents deserve to know. i can't just sit on that. it feels like i'm hiding it.

**No. Skipping the daycare group is not hiding it.**

You already decided not to sit on it. A CPS report is telling the people whose job is to check whether Leo is safe. If this happened at daycare or on a daycare outing, the director and licensing are the other parents’ kids’ version of that. That is disclosure. A parent-group post is a broadcast.

The “if I stay quiet and another kid gets hurt” feeling is the fear talking, not a missing step. Other parents do not get a safer kid from a thread. They get a story, Leo gets named in it, and Marcus gets a crowd to perform for. You already know he will call you hysterical. A group chat is where that version spreads.

What actually means you didn’t hide it:
- File the report today, like you said.
- If staff or a daycare event was involved, tell the director today. If they shrug, licensing.
- Leo does not go near water with Marcus on a phone.

You can live with not posting. You would have a much harder time living with turning Leo’s scare into group-chat evidence. The moral leftover is the report and real supervision, not an audience.
